vr.e: Candid means openly saying what you really think, so honest and direct is the match; a candid friend is never secretive or polite but vague.

vr.q: THOROUGH most nearly means:
vr.e: Thorough work covers every part of the job, so leaving nothing out fits; a thorough search is the opposite of one done in a great hurry.

vr.q: PLAUSIBLE most nearly means:
vr.e: A plausible excuse is one that could reasonably be true, so believable is right; plausible is the opposite of impossible.

vr.q: TEDIOUS most nearly means:
vr.e: A tedious chore drags on and wears you out with dullness, so long and boring fits; brief and lively is its opposite.

vr.q: DISPUTE most nearly means:
vr.e: To dispute a call or a claim is to argue against it and say it is not right, so to argue against is the match; someone who disputes a decision is doing the opposite of agreeing quickly.

vr.q: SUPERFICIAL most nearly means:
vr.e: Superficial means staying on the surface, so a superficial cut or a superficial friendship is shallow rather than deep.

vr.q: MEDIOCRE most nearly means:
vr.e: Mediocre means no better than middling, so only average fits; it is the opposite of clearly excellent.

vr.q: LENIENT most nearly means:
vr.e: A lenient teacher lets small things slide, so not strict; forgiving is the match, and strict and demanding is the opposite.

vr.q: ADMIRABLE most nearly means:
vr.e: Something admirable earns real respect and praise, so worth praising fits; barely acceptable is nearly its opposite.

vr.q: SKEPTICAL most nearly means:
vr.e: A skeptical listener is not convinced and wants proof, so doubting is right; trusting is the opposite attitude.

vr.q: Even though he wanted to keep arguing, Marcus had to ______ that his sister was right.
vr.e: To concede is to admit that someone else is right, which is what "had to" signals here; to deny or to insist that she was right would mean he never gave in.

vr.q: The principal stopped by our classroom to ______ the students for their hard work.
vr.e: To commend is to praise someone for what they have done, which is what hard work earns; to scold or to warn would be the opposite reaction.

vr.q: Because her own brother was racing, Mia could not serve as a ______ judge.
vr.e: A neutral judge favors neither side, and Mia would naturally want her brother to win; having a brother in the race would not stop her from being patient, careful, or capable.

vr.q: Ana shouted her answer before she had read the whole question — a ______ move she soon regretted.
vr.e: Hasty means done too quickly and with too little thought, which is exactly what answering before reading is; a patient or clever move would have been the opposite.

vr.q: Ms. Bell wrote a helpful ______ of my essay, naming both its strengths and its weaknesses.
vr.e: A critique is a careful judgement that weighs strong points against weak ones, which is what Ms. Bell wrote; an apology or an announcement judges nothing.

vr.q: Her apology sounded ______; anyone could tell she truly meant it.
vr.e: Sincere means truly meant, which matches the clue that she really meant it; a sarcastic apology is one that is not meant at all.

vr.q: Forgetting the tickets was a ______ that cost us an hour.
vr.e: A blunder is a careless mistake, and forgetting the tickets cost the group an hour; a bargain or a reward would be something good.

vr.q: The judges ______ each photograph before choosing a winner.
vr.e: To scrutinize is to examine something very closely, which is how judges pick a winner; judges who ignored the photographs could not choose at all.

vr.q: The coach said the plan had real ______ and was worth trying.
vr.e: Merit is real worth or value, so a plan with merit is worth trying; damage, delay, and silence would all be reasons to drop it.

vr.q: A ______ athlete, Nia plays goalkeeper, midfield, and forward equally well.
vr.e: Versatile means able to do many different things well, which is what playing three positions equally well shows; clumsy and nervous name weaknesses, not range.

vr.q: FLAW most nearly means:
vr.e: A flaw is a weak spot or fault, like a crack in a bowl; a reward, a journey, and a promise have nothing to do with imperfection.

vr.q: TRIVIAL most nearly means:
vr.e: Trivial details are so small that they hardly matter, so unimportant is the match.

vr.q: HARSH most nearly means:
vr.e: Harsh means rough or severe, as in a harsh winter or a harsh punishment; gentle is its opposite.

vr.q: APPROVE most nearly means:
vr.e: To approve something is to judge it good and agree to it, so to accept as good fits; to argue against it is the opposite.

vr.q: PRUDENT most nearly means:
vr.e: A prudent choice is a careful, sensible one that avoids needless risk, so careful and wise is right; bold and reckless is its opposite.

vr.q: SHODDY most nearly means:
vr.e: Shoddy goods are put together cheaply and badly, so poorly made fits; carefully built is the opposite.

vr.q: FLATTER most nearly means:
vr.e: To flatter is to pile on more praise than is deserved, often to get something; to blame unfairly is the opposite kind of remark.

vr.q: CONDEMN most nearly means:
vr.e: To condemn something is to declare that it is very wrong, so to strongly disapprove is the match; praising and celebrating point the other way.

vr.q: Ravi tends to ______ when he tells the story, so the fish he caught grows another foot longer every time.
vr.e: To exaggerate is to make something sound bigger than it really was, which is why the fish keeps growing with every telling.

vr.q: We were told not to ______ about our victory, no matter how proud we felt.
vr.e: To boast is to brag about your own success, exactly what proud winners were warned against; complaining and grumbling are what a losing team might do.

vr.q: Their plan was ______; one hard question and it fell apart.
vr.e: Flimsy means weak and easily broken, so a plan that collapses at the first hard question is flimsy; sturdy is its opposite.

vr.q: Before repairs began, an expert came to ______ the damage.
vr.e: To assess damage is to judge how bad it is before deciding what to do; an expert would not be sent for to ignore or enjoy it.

vr.q: Her excuse was ______: she had a doctor's note for that morning.
vr.e: A valid excuse is one that really holds up, and a doctor's note is solid proof; untrue would mean the opposite.

vr.q: Spending his whole allowance on one poster now seems ______ to Theo, who has nothing left for the class trip.
vr.e: Foolish means showing poor judgement, and Theo can now see that the poster was a bad use of his money; a wise choice would have left him enough for the trip.

vr.q: The ______ shopper compared prices at three stores before buying.
vr.e: A shrewd shopper judges value cleverly, which is why she checked three stores first; a careless shopper would have taken the first price offered.

vr.q: After years of service, the librarian was ______ of the town's highest honor.
vr.e: To be worthy of an honor is to deserve it, and years of service is exactly what earns one.

vr.q: The young pianist won wide ______ after her first concert.
vr.e: Acclaim is loud public praise, the natural result of a successful first concert; blame would follow a failure instead.

vr.q: BENEVOLENT most nearly means:
vr.e: Bene means “good,” and a benevolent neighbour wishes other people well, so kind and generous is the match; being strict about rules is a different quality entirely.

vr.q: MALICIOUS most nearly means:
vr.e: The prefix mal- means “bad,” so a malicious rumour is spread on purpose to hurt someone — meaning to do harm.

vr.q: DEJECTED most nearly means:
vr.e: De- means “down” and ject means “thrown,” so a dejected player walks off the field thrown down — low in spirits.

vr.q: ABRUPT most nearly means:
vr.e: An abrupt stop or an abrupt answer comes with no warning at all, so sudden fits; lengthy is closer to its opposite.

vr.q: OBSTRUCT most nearly means:
vr.e: Ob- means “against” and struct means “build,” so to obstruct a road is to put something in the way — to block it.

vr.q: RETRACT most nearly means:
vr.e: Re- means “back” and tract means “pull,” so a cat retracts its claws and a writer retracts a statement — both take back.

vr.q: CREDIBLE most nearly means:
vr.e: The root cred means “believe,” as in credit and incredible, so a credible witness is a believable one.

vr.q: NOVICE most nearly means:
vr.e: Nov- means “new,” so a novice is someone new to an activity — a beginner, whatever else she may also be.

vr.q: SURPLUS most nearly means:
vr.e: Sur- means “over,” so a surplus is what is left over once everyone has enough — an extra amount, the exact opposite of a shortage of supplies.

vr.q: VERDICT most nearly means:
vr.e: Ver- means “truth” and dict means “speak,” so a verdict is what the jury speaks at the end of a trial; the speeches and the stories all come before it.

vr.q: The team watched the little robot ______ and waited for its lights to reappear.
vr.e: Sub- means “under,” so to submerge is to go down under the water, which is why the crew has to wait for the lights to come back into view.

vr.q: The bats slept in a cool ______ chamber the cavers reached only after an hour’s climb down.
vr.e: Sub- means “under” and terra means “earth,” so a subterranean chamber lies underground at the bottom of a long climb; bats would not sleep in a flooded one.

vr.q: Announcing the winner before the last runner had finished turned out to be ______: the trophy had to be handed to someone else.
vr.e: Pre- means “before,” so something premature happens too early; the announcement was clearly not harmless, since the trophy had to change hands.

vr.q: It is rude to ______ your grandmother in front of guests, even when you are sure she is wrong.
vr.e: Contra- means “against” and dict means “speak,” so to contradict is to speak against what someone has just said — which is what makes it rude here.

vr.q: The ______ of a whole week at the beach kept the twins cheerful all through exam season.
vr.e: Pro- means “forward” and spect means “look,” so a prospect is something you look forward to; a penalty or a disappointment would not keep anyone cheerful.

vr.q: Because the harvest was so large, the country was able to ______ tons of rice to its neighbors.
vr.e: Ex- means “out” and port means “carry,” so to export rice is to carry it out of the country to buyers elsewhere.

vr.q: The jeweler offered to ______ our initials on the inside of the ring.
vr.e: Scrib and script mean “write,” so to inscribe initials on a ring is to write or carve them into it.

vr.q: Workers set out barrels to ______ traffic around the flooded street.
vr.e: Di- means “aside” and vert means “turn,” so to divert traffic is to turn it aside — here, around the flooded street.

vr.q: One strong kick was enough to ______ the swimmer all the way to the far wall.
vr.e: Pro- means “forward” and pel means “drive,” so to propel the swimmer is to drive her forward to the far wall.

vr.q: Ms. Reyes asked Dev to speak up, because his answer was barely ______ at the back of the room.
vr.e: Aud means “hear” and -ible means “able to be,” so audible means able to be heard — which is why Dev is asked to speak up.

vr.q: EJECT most nearly means:
vr.e: E- means “out” and ject means “throw,” so to eject is to throw or force something out — the opposite of joining it together.

vr.q: SPECTACLE most nearly means:
vr.e: Spect means “look,” so a spectacle is something people stop to look at — a remarkable sight, not a sound.

vr.q: MANUSCRIPT most nearly means:
vr.e: Manu means “hand” and script means “write,” so a manuscript is the author’s own written text, before any printing happens.

vr.q: RUPTURE most nearly means:
vr.e: Rupt means “break,” as in erupt and interrupt, so a rupture in a pipe is a break in it.

vr.q: AVERT most nearly means:
vr.e: A- means “away” and vert means “turn,” so you avert your eyes by turning them away.

vr.q: MAGNITUDE most nearly means:
vr.e: Magn- means “great,” as in magnify, so the magnitude of an earthquake is how great it is.

vr.q: FLUENT most nearly means:
vr.e: Flu means “flow,” as in fluid, so fluent speech flows easily; the word is about talking, not about running, lifting, or drawing.

vr.q: VACANT most nearly means:
vr.e: Vac means “empty,” as in vacuum and vacate, so a vacant seat has nobody in it — the opposite of crowded.

vr.q: She had forgotten to mention the party, so she squeezed it into a ______ after she had already signed her name.
vr.e: Post- means “after” and script means “write,” so a postscript is added after the letter is finished and signed; a preface would come first instead.

vr.q: The dentist used a small tool to ______ the loose tooth.
vr.e: Ex- means “out” and tract means “pull,” so to extract the loose tooth is to pull it out.

vr.q: The whale rose to the surface to ______ a spray of air and water.
vr.e: Ex- means “out” and pel means “drive,” so to expel the spray is to drive it out of the blowhole.

vr.q: The radio tower can ______ a signal for a hundred miles.
vr.e: Trans- means “across” and mit means “send,” so the tower sends a signal across a hundred miles.

vr.q: The hospital needed a ______ receptionist, because half the families who came in spoke only Spanish.
vr.e: Bi- means “two” and lingua means “language,” so a bilingual receptionist can speak with the Spanish-speaking families as well as the English-speaking ones; being punctual or courteous would not solve that problem.

vr.q: The sign warns drivers to stop for any ______ in the crosswalk.
vr.e: Ped means “foot,” so a pedestrian is a person travelling on foot — exactly who a crosswalk is meant for.

vr.q: The Romans built a stone ______ across the valley, and the city’s fountains ran for the first time.
vr.e: Aqua means “water” and duct means “lead,” so an aqueduct leads water into the city, which is why the fountains could finally run.

vr.q: A single lantern was enough to ______ the whole tent.
vr.e: Lumin means “light,” as in luminous, so to illuminate the tent is to light it up.

vr.q: Her second jump was so long that it seemed to ______ the school record.
vr.e: Sur- means “above,” so to surpass the school record is to go beyond it — her jump was longer than the old best.

vr.q: FRUGAL most nearly means:
vr.e: Frugal describes someone who spends carefully and avoids waste, so wasting money is its opposite; being frugal says nothing about how much money a person was born with or about giving it away.

vr.q: INQUISITIVE most nearly means:
vr.e: An inquisitive person asks questions and wants to find things out; fear, boasting, and refusing to change are different traits altogether.

vr.q: ARROGANT most nearly means:
vr.e: Arrogant means having too high an opinion of yourself — the opposite of shy, and unrelated to forgiving or to being careful.

vr.q: STERN most nearly means:
vr.e: A stern teacher looks and sounds serious and expects the rules to be kept; gentleness, cheerfulness, and hesitation all point the other way.

vr.q: DILIGENT most nearly means:
vr.e: A diligent worker keeps at a job carefully and steadily, so giving up quickly and working carelessly are its opposites; sharing is a different trait.

vr.q: EARNEST most nearly means:
vr.e: Earnest means you truly mean what you say and say it seriously, which rules out joking, rudeness, and boredom.

vr.q: INDIGNANT most nearly means:
vr.e: Indignant is the particular anger you feel when something is unjust. Delight, curiosity, and worry are not anger at all.

vr.q: ENVIOUS most nearly means:
vr.e: An envious person looks at what someone else has and wishes it were hers, so being glad about another's good luck is the opposite feeling; fear and pride are different feelings altogether.

vr.q: ENTHUSIASTIC most nearly means:
vr.e: An enthusiastic helper throws herself into the job because she is genuinely excited about it, which rules out boredom, cool calm, and polite distance.

vr.q: CAUTIOUS most nearly means:
vr.e: A cautious driver slows down before a blind corner, so cautious is the opposite of taking chances or rushing, and it says nothing about being friendly.

vr.q: Even after his cousins offered to pay him back the next day, Marcus refused to lend a single dollar, and the family found his ______ behavior hard to forgive.
vr.e: “Hard to forgive” marks the word as criticism, and refusing a loan that would be repaid the next day costs him nothing — so the praising words thrifty, frugal, and practical (all meaning wise with money) cannot fit; only stingy, which means mean about giving, does.

vr.q: Nobody saw who took the last cupcake, but the ______ grin Rico wore when the empty plate was found told everyone exactly who had.
vr.e: The grin that gives him away shows he got the cupcake by quiet trickery, which is what sly means; honest is the opposite, gracious describes warm manners, and someone who is puzzled has not just pulled off a trick.

vr.q: The inventor's claims were ______: she said the new battery might last an hour longer, not that it would change the world.
vr.e: Claiming only an extra hour rather than changing the world keeps her claims small and unexaggerated, which is what modest means here; boastful and grand describe exactly the big claims she avoids, and her careful wording is the opposite of reckless.

vr.q: When the rest of the team stopped speaking to Priya after the missed penalty, Dana walked home with her as she always had; nobody who knew Dana was surprised at how ______ she was.
vr.e: Standing by a friend when everyone else turns away is faithfulness, which is what loyal means; the sentence is not about bragging, about being liked by the crowd, or about running out of patience.

vr.q: His advice was accurate but so ______ that it stung: “Your essay is dull, and you never checked the spelling.”
vr.e: “Stung” rules out gentle and tactful, and the quoted remark names two specific faults, which rules out vague; blunt means honest in a way that spares no feelings.

vr.q: Nobody had asked Mr. Odile to drive two hours with the costumes the cast had forgotten, and the cast was so ______ that they made him a card and clapped when he walked in.
vr.e: Making a card and clapping for someone who drove two hours unasked is a show of thanks, which is what grateful means; annoyance and indifference would show no thanks at all, and nothing about the drive puzzles them.

vr.q: The assembly opened with a ______ minute of silence for the school's founder, and even the youngest students stopped fidgeting.
vr.e: A minute of silence that makes small children go still is grave and dignified, which rules out festive, playful, and casual.

vr.q: Ms. Ortiz did not excuse the late homework, but her voice was so ______ that Danny came away feeling understood rather than scolded.
vr.e: “Feeling understood rather than scolded” rules out severe and mocking, and indifference would leave him feeling nothing; sympathetic means sharing in how someone else feels.

vr.q: The box of old camp photographs left Grandma smiling and ______, saying again and again how much she missed those summers by the lake.
vr.e: She is smiling and speaking fondly of what she misses, which rules out bitter and anxious; nothing is being waited for, so not impatient. Nostalgic is exactly this fond longing for the past.

vr.q: By the last mile of the hike Ana had stopped chattering altogether, and her answers came out in a ______ mumble.
vr.e: Falling silent and mumbling at the end of a long hike shows worn-out tiredness, which is what weary means; a cheerful or playful hiker would still be talking, and nothing on the trail has alarmed her.

vr.q: BOASTFUL most nearly means:
vr.e: A boastful person keeps announcing how good he is; complaining, fear, and generosity are unrelated traits.

vr.q: GRACIOUS most nearly means:
vr.e: Gracious describes warm good manners, the direct opposite of coldly rude, and it has nothing to do with confusion or humor.

vr.q: RESENTFUL most nearly means:
vr.e: Resentful is the sour anger left behind by treatment you think was unfair; gratitude is its opposite, and eagerness and puzzlement are not anger.

vr.q: MELANCHOLY most nearly means:
vr.e: Melancholy is a low, lingering sadness, so humor, energy, and alertness all miss it.

vr.q: GRIM most nearly means:
vr.e: Grim describes something stern and cheerless; hopeful, silly, and welcoming are all the opposite in feeling.

vr.q: APOLOGETIC most nearly means:
vr.e: Apologetic means showing that you regret something you did; pride, anger, and curiosity carry no regret.

vr.q: SCORNFUL most nearly means:
vr.e: Scorn is contempt, so scornful means treating something as beneath you — the opposite of admiring, and unrelated to helpfulness or uncertainty.

vr.q: DEFIANT most nearly means:
vr.e: Defiant means openly standing against an order, the opposite of obedient; amusement and gratitude are different feelings entirely.

vr.q: Though the whole town praised her invention, Maya stayed ______, insisting that her science teacher deserved as much credit as she did.
vr.e: She insists on sharing the credit, which rules out smug, and insisting aloud is not timid; she plainly cares, so not indifferent. Humble means not thinking too highly of yourself.

vr.q: After the win, Trent's grin was ______, and he reminded everyone yet again that he had predicted the score exactly.
vr.e: Reminding everyone “yet again” of his own correct prediction is self-satisfied, not gracious; he is neither sorry (apologetic) nor worried (anxious) after winning.

vr.q: The kitten's ______ streak showed the moment she batted every pencil off the desk and darted away with her tail high.
vr.e: Knocking pencils down harms nobody, so vicious (cruel) is far too strong; she is causing trouble, so not obedient, and darting off tail-high is not timid. Mischievous means playfully naughty.

vr.q: Two goals behind at half time, Coach stayed ______, telling the players the comeback was still theirs for the taking.
vr.e: He encourages the team, which rules out gloomy and furious, and “still theirs for the taking” shows he is sure rather than uncertain; optimistic means expecting things to turn out well.

vr.q: Ravi had been certain he had failed the audition, so when the cast list went up with his name on it, he sat down on the steps looking utterly ______.
vr.e: Seeing his name after expecting the worst lifts a weight off him, which is what relieved means; alarm, annoyance, and disappointment would all follow bad news, not good.

vr.q: Rather than saying the painting was ugly, Nina gave a ______ reply, praising its colors before suggesting one change.
vr.e: “Rather than saying it was ugly” and the praise that comes first rule out blunt and rude, and she says nothing about herself, so not boastful; tactful means honest without wounding.

vr.q: The old dog was ______, nudging Nora's hand until she petted him and then settling his head in her lap.
vr.e: He seeks Nora out for petting, so he is not indifferent, and resting his head in her lap shows trust, which rules out hostile and fearful; affectionate means showing fondness.

vr.q: With the results due any minute, Dev chewed his sleeve and kept checking the clock; he was plainly ______, certain the news would be bad.
vr.e: Being “certain the news would be bad” is worry, not boredom, and the sleeve-chewing and clock-watching rule out relaxed and delighted; anxious means uneasy about what is coming.

vr.q: The review was sharply ______, listing every flaw in the play and praising almost nothing.
vr.e: Listing every flaw and praising almost nothing rules out admiring and cheerful, and the word “sharply” rules out neutral; critical here means fault-finding.

vr.q: DISCRETION most nearly means:
c: the power to decide for yourself
a rule that must always be followed
vr.e: When a trip is “left to the principal's discretion,” she has the power to decide; a rule that must be followed is the opposite of leaving a choice to someone.

vr.q: UNANIMOUS most nearly means:
c: agreed to by every single member
decided by one person in charge
put off until a later meeting
vr.e: A unanimous vote is one in which everyone agrees. The look-alike word is anonymous, which means the name is not known.

vr.q: CONSPICUOUS most nearly means:
c: acting in a sneaky, guilty way
vr.e: A conspicuous stain is one everyone sees at once. Suspicious (sneaky) and conscientious (careful) are the two look-alike words that do not mean the same thing.

vr.q: BENIGN most nearly means:
vr.e: A benign remark or a benign old dog does no harm; none of the other choices carries the idea of harmlessness.

vr.q: PREDICAMENT most nearly means:
c: a hard spot to get out of
a promise made in front of a crowd
a guess about what will happen next
a long delay before an event
vr.e: Being locked out in the rain with no phone is a predicament — a situation you cannot easily escape. The look-alike word is prediction, a guess about the future.

vr.q: REMINISCE most nearly means:
c: to remind someone of a chore
to plan carefully for next year
to talk fondly about times gone by
vr.e: To reminisce is to look back and share memories, the way grandparents do about their childhood; reminding, apologizing, and planning all point at the present or future.

vr.q: WANE most nearly means:
c: to get smaller little by little
vr.e: Interest that wanes fades bit by bit, the way a waning moon shrinks each night; its partner word wax means to grow.

vr.q: LITERAL most nearly means:
c: spoken in a very loud voice
having to do with books and authors
taking words in their exact meaning
vr.e: The literal meaning of “raining cats and dogs” would be actual animals falling from the sky. Literary, the look-alike word, is about books.

vr.q: SUBORDINATE most nearly means:
vr.e: In “cost was a subordinate concern,” cost mattered less than the main issue; something subordinate ranks below, never above or equal.

vr.q: COMPACT most nearly means:
c: spread out over a wide area
vr.e: A compact kitchen fits everything into a small area; compact says nothing about softness, single use, or wide spread.

vr.q: Starting a bakery takes more ______ than most people expect: ovens, rent, and flour must all be paid for before the first loaf is sold.
vr.e: Capital is the money and resources needed to start or run a business, which is exactly what the ovens, rent, and flour require.

vr.q: Mr. Alvarez graded the ______ of each essay — the ideas and the evidence — rather than the neatness of the handwriting.
vr.e: Here content means what is inside the essay — the ideas and the evidence — rather than how much was written (volume); this is a different meaning from “content with her meal,” which means satisfied.

vr.q: Our science teacher wrote the ______ “habitat” on the board and asked us to explain what it names.
vr.e: A term is a word or expression used for something — a different meaning from a school term or the terms of a contract.

vr.q: Grandma keeps the first ______ of the old encyclopedia, the one covering A through C, beside her chair.
vr.e: A volume is one book of a set; “the one covering A through C” rules out the loudness and the amount meanings.

vr.q: When the storm knocked out the power, the fire department ______ assistance to every family on the block, delivering water and blankets before midnight.
vr.e: To render assistance is to give it, which is exactly what delivering water and blankets describes; refusing or suspending help would mean the opposite, and to eradicate something is to wipe it out completely.

vr.q: The museum applied for a ______ from the city and used the money to repair its leaking roof.
vr.e: A grant is a sum of money given for a purpose; “used the money” shows this is the noun, not the verb “to grant permission.”

vr.q: Because no ferry ran on Sundays, the team had to ______ a boat to reach the island for the tournament.
vr.e: To charter a boat or a bus is to hire it for private use — the verb sense, not the city charter that is a founding document.

vr.q: Ticket sales began to ______ in the third week, dropping from four hundred a night to barely fifty.
vr.e: The numbers fall from 400 to 50, so decline here means to go steadily down, not to turn down an invitation.

vr.q: The vet spoke in a ______ voice and moved slowly, and the frightened kitten stopped shaking.
vr.e: Tender here means gentle and kind, which is what calms the kitten; the sore-to-the-touch meaning of tender would not describe a voice.

vr.q: The old radio crackled with so much ______ that we could not make out a single word of the weather report.
vr.e: Static is the crackling noise that blocks a radio signal — a noun, and a different meaning from static as “not changing.”

vr.q: EXPLOIT most nearly means:
c: to take unfair advantage of someone
vr.e: An employer who exploits workers profits from them by paying unfairly; praising, repairing, and handing over involve no unfair use.

vr.q: STRIVE most nearly means:
c: to wait for someone else to act
to try hard over a long time
vr.e: To strive for a goal is to keep making real effort toward it; each of the other choices describes not making that effort.

vr.q: DISCIPLINE most nearly means:
c: a talent a person is born with
a piece of unexpected good luck
vr.e: The discipline to practice every day is trained control over your own behavior, not a mood, a natural gift, or luck.

vr.q: FEISTY most nearly means:
c: polite and quiet in a crowd
vr.e: A feisty puppy barks boldly at a much larger dog — full of spirit and unwilling to back down.

vr.q: PROMPT most nearly means:
vr.e: A prompt reply arrives right away, so prompt is about speed; care, repetition, and group size are different ideas.

vr.q: CULTIVATE most nearly means:
c: to grow and care for over time
to cut down and clear away
vr.e: Farmers cultivate crops and people cultivate friendships — both mean tending something so it develops; cutting down is closer to the opposite.

vr.q: DOMESTIC most nearly means:
c: built a very long time ago
having to do with the home
vr.e: Domestic chores are household chores and a domestic animal is one kept at home; the other choices all point away from the home.

vr.q: RETALIATE most nearly means:
c: to strike back after being harmed
to go back and fetch something
to say sorry and make peace
vr.e: A team that trips a player after being tripped retaliates. Retrieve (fetch) and retreat (pull back) are the look-alike words.

vr.q: Two coaches told Nadia the record was out of reach, but she remained ______ and trained every morning anyway.
vr.e: “Trained every morning anyway” shows she held firmly to her purpose, which is what resolute means; the other three say nothing about determination.

vr.q: The class had plenty of theories about the missing mascot but no ______ proof — no photograph, no footprint, nothing they could point to.
vr.e: Tangible proof is solid evidence you can touch or point to, which is exactly what the missing photograph and footprint would have been.

vr.q: A classroom rule that punishes every mistake can ______ the very curiosity the teacher hopes to build.
vr.e: To stifle something is to smother or hold it back, and a rule that punishes every mistake crushes the curiosity the teacher wants; cultivating curiosity would grow it instead, exploiting means using something unfairly for your own gain, and nothing here is being measured.

vr.q: The general finally learned that his most trusted messenger had been ______ all along, quietly carrying the battle plans to the enemy.
vr.e: Treacherous here means disloyal — betraying the trust placed in him — a different sense from a treacherous mountain road. Conspicuous is ruled out by “quietly.”

vr.q: The offer sounded ______ to Mom: a free bicycle for anyone who simply forwarded the message to ten friends.
vr.e: Something dubious is doubtful and not to be trusted, which is how an offer that seems too good to be true sounds; the other three say nothing about doubt.

vr.q: The umpires had to ______ the game in the fourth inning, and both teams waited under the bleachers until the lightning had passed.
vr.e: To suspend something is to stop it for a while, which is what umpires do when lightning arrives; extending, announcing, or repeating the game would all keep it going. Suspend can also mean to hang something up.

vr.q: The injured owl was carried to a bird ______ outside town, where volunteers fed it by hand until it was strong enough to hunt again.
vr.e: A sanctuary is a safe place where something is protected, which is what a refuge for hurt birds is; a laboratory is for experiments, a boundary is a line, and a predicament is a situation rather than a place.

vr.q: By noon there was not a ______ of snow left on the field; the grass was green and dry from one end to the other.
vr.e: A trace is the tiny amount left behind, so “not a trace” means none at all, which fits grass that is green and dry from end to end. Trace can also mean to copy a drawing through thin paper.

vr.q: After the third sandwich went missing from the counter, Dad began to ______ that the new puppy was not as innocent as she looked.
vr.e: To suspect is to start believing something is true before you have proof, which is what the missing sandwiches lead Dad to think about the puppy; he is not telling anyone, he is far from certain, and he plainly has not forgotten.

qr.q: A garden club plants 28 bulbs, and 3/4 of them bloom. How many bulbs bloom?
qr.e: Find 3/4 of 28: 28÷4=7, and 7×3=21 bulbs.

qr.q: Two runners complete 5/6 and 7/9 of a relay. Which runner completed more?
qr.e: Use eighteenths: 5/6=15/18 and 7/9=14/18, so the 5/6 runner completed more.

qr.q: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 8 muffins. At the same rate, how many cups are needed for 20 muffins?
Four notebooks cost $10. What is the cost per notebook?
3/5 of a class is 18 students. How many students are in the whole class?
qr.e: 18 is 3 parts, so 1 part is 6; 5 parts = 30.

qr.q: The ratio of red to blue marbles is 2:3. If there are 25 marbles total, how many are red?
qr.e: There are 5 equal parts; 25 ÷ 5 = 5, and 2 parts = 10.

qr.q: Mia read 2/3 of a 60-page book, then read half of the pages that remained. How many pages are still unread?
qr.e: She read 40 pages, then 10 more of the 20 remaining, leaving 10.

qr.q: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed?
A trail is 2/3 paved and 1/4 gravel, with no overlap. What fraction of the trail is paved or gravel?
A 5 1/2-yard ribbon loses 2 3/4 yards. How much ribbon remains?
qr.e: Rename 5 1/2 as 5 2/4, regroup, and subtract 2 3/4 to get 2 3/4 yards.

qr.q: How many 1/8-cup servings are in 3/4 cup?
qr.e: 3/4 = 6/8, so there are six 1/8-cup servings.

qr.q: A paint recipe mixes yellow and blue in a 4:5 ratio. Which batch keeps the same ratio?
qr.e: Multiply both parts of 4:5 by 3 to get the equivalent ratio 12:15.

qr.q: Museum tickets cost $6 each. A family spends $24 on x tickets. How many tickets does the family buy?
qr.e: The equation is 6x=24. Divide both sides by 6 to get x=4 tickets.

qr.q: A baker needs the fraction of a pie that is closest to one whole pie. Which amount is closest to 1?
qr.e: Compare each gap from 1. The gap for 9/10 is only 1/10, smaller than the other gaps.

qr.q: Five pens cost $7.50. At the same rate, how much do 8 pens cost?
2/5 of the students are boys. If 18 students are girls, how many students are in the class?
qr.e: Girls are 3/5 of the class. If 3/5 = 18, then the whole is 30.

qr.q: A 48-seat bus has 25% of its seats reserved. How many seats are reserved?
qr.e: Twenty-five percent is one fourth, and 48÷4=12 reserved seats.

qr.q: A 6/8-mile route is shortened to an equivalent fraction on a map label. Which label matches the route?
qr.e: Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 6/8=3/4 mile.

qr.q: A school has 18 violins and 12 cellos. What is the ratio of violins to cellos in simplest form?
qr.e: 18:12 simplifies by dividing both numbers by 6 to 3:2.

qr.q: A tank is 3/4 full and contains 18 gallons. How many gallons does it hold when full?
qr.e: 18 ÷ 3 × 4 = 24 gallons.

qr.q: Store A sells 6 markers for $9. Store B sells 10 markers for $14. Which store has the lower cost per marker?
qr.e: Store A is $1.50 each; Store B is $1.40 each.

qr.q: A tile pattern has 2, 6, 18, and 54 tiles, tripling each time. How many tiles are in the next design?
qr.e: The rule is multiply by 3, so 54×3=162 tiles.

qr.q: Three quiz scores are 8, 10, and 15. What is their average?
qr.e: Add the scores to get 33, then divide by 3: 33÷3=11.

qr.q: The ratio of cats to dogs is 7:3. If there are 50 animals total, how many are cats?
qr.e: There are 10 equal parts; 50 ÷ 10 = 5, so cats = 7 × 5 = 35.

qr.q: A recipe uses 4/5 cup of milk and 1/2 cup less water. How much water does it use?
A 2 1/4-liter jug is used to fill 3/4-liter bottles. How many full bottles can it fill?
qr.e: Rename 2 1/4 as 9/4. Then (9/4)÷(3/4)=3 full bottles.

qr.q: On a map, 1 inch represents 6 miles. Two towns are 3.5 inches apart. How far apart are they?
A 7-by-7 photo display uses one tile per space. How many tiles are needed?
qr.e: A photo display has 7 rows of 7 tiles, so 7×7=49.

qr.q: An 81-square-inch mosaic is a square. How long is one side?
qr.e: A square with area 81 has side √81=9.

qr.q: A square game board uses 64 small tiles. How many tiles are in each row?
qr.e: The side length is √64=8 tiles.

qr.q: A square flower bed covers 50 square feet. Between which whole-number side lengths is its side?
qr.e: 7²=49 and 8²=64, so √50 lies between 7 and 8.

qr.q: Which patio tile count can be arranged as a perfect square array?
qr.e: 36 makes a 6-by-6 array; the other counts do not make equal rows and columns.

qr.q: A square has side length 12 cm. What is its area?
qr.e: Area of a square is side × side: 12×12=144 cm².

qr.q: A square has area 81 square inches. What is its perimeter?
qr.e: The side is √81=9; perimeter =4×9=36 in.

qr.q: Corner tiles in a growing display number 1, 4, 9, 16, ... . What is the next count?
qr.e: The counts are square arrays 1²,2²,3²,4²; next is 5²=25.

qr.q: Choosing one odd bead and one even bead gives a total that is always:
qr.e: Odd + even is always odd.

qr.q: A theater sells 234 tickets. Is that number divisible by 3?
c: No; it does not end in 3
qr.e: A number is divisible by 3 when its digit sum is divisible by 3. 2+3+4=9.

qr.q: 53 supplies are packed in boxes of 6. How many supplies are left over?
qr.e: 6×8=48, leaving 5 supplies.

qr.q: 42 flags are placed in equal rows. Which row size works with no flags left over?
qr.e: 42÷6=7, so rows of 6 work exactly.

qr.q: A 100-square mural is arranged in a square. How many squares are on one side?
qr.e: √100=10, so a 10-by-10 mural has 100 squares.

qr.q: A square seating section holds 121 seats in equal rows. How many seats are in each row?
An 8-by-8 mural and a 2-to-the-6th grid both cover how many cells?
qr.e: 8²=64 and 2⁶=64, so both cover 64 cells.

qr.q: A shelf holds 40 books. Which square numbers is that count between?
qr.e: 6²=36 and 7²=49, so 40 lies between them.

qr.q: Lanterns are arranged in rows of 5, 9, 17, 33, ... . What is the next row size?
qr.e: Each term is double the previous term minus 1: 33×2−1=65.

qr.q: Bells ring every 6 and 8 minutes. After ringing together now, when do they first ring together again?
qr.e: The least common multiple of 6 and 8 is 24.

qr.q: 18 red and 24 blue ribbons are cut into the largest equal bundles with no ribbon left. How many ribbons are in each bundle?
qr.e: The greatest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6.

qr.q: A 42-card code is factored into primes. What is its greatest prime factor?
qr.e: 42=2×3×7, so the greatest prime factor is 7.

qr.q: If n is odd, which expression must be even?
qr.e: An odd number plus 3 (an odd number) is even.

qr.q: Three consecutive locker numbers total 36. What is the middle locker number?
qr.e: The three numbers are 11,12,13; the middle is 12.

qr.q: A museum expects about 198 visitors in each of 6 groups. About how many visitors is that?
A rectangular screen is 4 units by 3 units. The expression 4²+3² equals:
A point starts at (2,3). It moves 4 units right and 2 units down. Where does it end?
qr.e: 2+4=6 and 3−2=1, so the point is (6,1).

qr.q: A display uses factor tags 1, 2, 4, and 8—and no others. What is the display number?
qr.e: Those are exactly the positive factors of 8.

qr.q: Which square display count is greater than 70 but less than 90?
What is the volume of a rectangular prism that is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide, and 3 cm high?
qr.e: Volume = length × width × height = 5×4×3 = 60.

qr.q: A rectangular prism has volume 96 cm³. Its length is 8 cm and width is 4 cm. What is its height?
A cube has edge length 4 inches. What is its volume?
A rectangle is 7 m long and 5 m wide. What is its perimeter?
qr.e: Perimeter = 2(7+5)=24.

qr.q: A triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
Two angles form a straight line. One angle is 125°. What is the other angle?
qr.e: Angles on a straight line total 180°; 180−125=55.

qr.q: A square window is tested for reflection symmetry. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
qr.e: A square matches across its vertical, horizontal, and two diagonal folds, for 4 lines.

qr.q: If only the height of a rectangular prism is doubled, its volume becomes:
qr.e: Volume is proportional to height, so doubling height doubles volume.

qr.q: A rectangle has vertices (1,1), (5,1), (5,4), and (1,4). What is its area?
qr.e: Width = 4 and height = 3, so area = 12.

qr.q: Five daily readings are 6, 8, 9, 12, and 15. What is the mean reading?
qr.e: The readings total 50; 50÷5=10.

qr.q: The ordered locker numbers are 3, 4, 8, 10, and 14. What is the median locker number?
qr.e: With five ordered values, the third value is the median: 8.

qr.q: Recorded temperatures range from a low of 11° to a high of 20°. What is the temperature range?
qr.e: Range is high minus low: 20−11=9°.

qr.q: What is the volume of a rectangular prism measuring 9 by 2 by 5?
A cube has volume 125 cubic units. What is the length of one edge?
A rectangle has area 48 square units and width 6. What is its length?
A rectangle has perimeter 30 units and length 9 units. What is its width?
A triangle has angles 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
qr.e: Triangle angles total 180°; 180−110=70.

qr.q: The mean of four numbers is 18. Three of the numbers total 50. What is the fourth number?
qr.e: The total of all four is 72; 72−50=22.

qr.q: Seven ordered scores are 2, 5, 7, 9, 12, 15, and 20. What is the median score?
qr.e: The fourth of seven ordered values is the median, so the median is 9.

qr.q: A color poll records 4 red, 6 blue, 8 green, and 5 yellow votes. The most chosen color received how many votes?
qr.e: Green has the greatest frequency with 8 votes, so the modal response count is 8.

qr.q: A bag has 3 red, 2 blue, and 5 green marbles. What is the probability of choosing a blue marble?
qr.e: There are 10 marbles total and 2 are blue: 2/10=1/5.

qr.q: Using the same bag, what is the probability of choosing a marble that is NOT red?
qr.e: 7 of the 10 marbles are not red.

qr.q: If both the length and width of a rectangle are doubled, its area becomes:
qr.e: Doubling both dimensions multiplies area by 2×2=4.

qr.q: If the length of a rectangular prism is doubled while width and height stay the same, its volume becomes:
qr.e: Volume is proportional to length.

qr.q: A map point at (3,−2) is reflected across a vertical mirror on the y-axis. What is the reflected point?
qr.e: Reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of x and keeps y, giving (−3,−2).

qr.q: The numbers 4, 5, 5, 6 have mean 5. If 20 is added to the data set, what happens to the mean?
qr.e: Adding a value much larger than the old mean raises the mean.

qr.q: Which measure is usually affected more by one extremely large outlier?
qr.e: The mean uses every value and is pulled toward an extreme outlier.

qr.q: A gardener has 3/4 cup of soil and fills pots with 1/8 cup each. How many pots can be filled?
qr.e: Rename 3/4 as 6/8, so six 1/8-cup pots can be filled.

qr.q: The ratio of boys to girls is 3:5. If there are 32 students total, how many are girls?
qr.e: There are 8 parts; 32÷8=4, and 5 parts = 20.

qr.q: A 12-ounce box costs $3.60. What is the cost per ounce?
A square mosaic uses 144 tiles in equal rows and columns. How many tiles are on one side?
qr.e: The side length is √144=12 because 12×12=144.

qr.q: A designer checks tile counts 49, 64, 72, and 81 for square arrays. Which count cannot form a square array?
qr.e: 49=7², 64=8², and 81=9²; 72 is not a perfect square.

qr.q: A prism has volume 180 cm³, length 10 cm, and width 6 cm. What is its height?
A rectangle has area 54 square units and length 9. What is its perimeter?
qr.e: Width=54÷9=6; perimeter=2(9+6)=30.

qr.q: A triangle has two equal angles of 55°. What is the third angle?
The mean of 12, 14, 16, and x is 15. What is x?
qr.e: A mean of 15 for 4 numbers means total 60; 60−42=18.

qr.q: A spinner has 8 equal sections: 3 red, 3 blue, 2 green. What is the probability of NOT landing on green?
qr.e: 6 of 8 sections are not green: 6/8=3/4.

qr.q: A student doubles the number of pages read each week: 3, 6, 12, 24, ... . How many pages come next?
qr.e: Each term doubles, so 24×2=48 pages.

qr.q: A supply count must be divisible by both 4 and 6. Which count works?
qr.e: 24÷4=6 and 24÷6=4, so 24 is divisible by both numbers.

qr.q: A jar is 2/3 full. After 8 cups are removed, it is 1/3 full. What is the jar's full capacity?
qr.e: The removed 8 cups equals 1/3 of the jar, so full capacity is 24.

qr.q: A runner travels 7.5 miles in 1.5 hours. What is the average rate?
A paint mixture uses blue and white in a 2:5 ratio. If 21 cups are mixed, how many cups are blue?
qr.e: There are 7 parts; 21÷7=3, so blue = 2×3 = 6.

qr.q: A 9-by-9 game board has 81 spaces. Which expression has the same value as the number of spaces?
qr.e: The board has 9²=81 spaces, and 3⁴=81.

qr.q: A square display uses 70 tiles. Between which two whole-number side lengths would its side lie?
qr.e: Because 8²=64 and 9²=81, √70 lies between 8 and 9.

qr.q: A number is divisible by 2, 3, and 5. Which could be the number?
qr.e: 30 is divisible by 2, 3, and 5.

qr.q: A fence-post pattern uses 4, 7, 13, and 25 posts. The increases double. How many posts come next?
qr.e: The increases are +3,+6,+12, so the next increase is +24 and 25+24=49.

qr.q: A rectangular prism is 6 by 5 by 4. If its height is cut in half, what is the new volume?
qr.e: Original volume is 120; halving height halves volume to 60.

qr.q: A square has perimeter 36 cm. What is its area?
qr.e: Each side is 9; area = 9² = 81.

qr.q: A right-angle art frame has one angle of 38°. What is the other angle?
qr.e: A right angle totals 90°, so 90−38=52°.

qr.q: Five supply trays contain an average of 14 items. How many items are in the trays altogether?
qr.e: Total equals mean×number of trays: 14×5=70 items.

qr.q: The ordered values are 3, 6, 9, x, and 15. Which value of x keeps the median at 9?
qr.e: With x=12, the ordered list is 3,6,9,12,15, whose middle value is 9.

qr.q: A fair number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
qr.e: The favorable outcomes are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6=1/3.

qr.q: A point at (-2,4) moves 5 units right. What is the new point?
qr.e: -2+5=3, so the point is (3,4).

qr.q: A 60-page book is read at 12 pages per day. After 3 days, what fraction of the book remains unread?
qr.e: 36 pages are read, leaving 24; 24/60=2/5.

qr.q: A box of 6 granola bars costs $3.00. At that rate, what is the cost of one granola bar?
qr.e: The 6 bars share the $3.00 evenly, so one bar costs $3.00 divided by 6 = $0.50.

qr.q: A necklace uses 2 red beads for every 3 white beads. The necklace has 6 red beads. How many white beads does it have?
qr.e: The 6 red beads make 3 groups of 2, and each group comes with 3 white beads, so there are 3 x 3 = 9 white beads.

qr.q: In a basket of red and green apples, the ratio of red apples to green apples is 3:4. Which statement must be true?
c: 3 out of every 4 apples are red.
There are exactly 3 red apples and 4 green apples.
4 out of every 7 apples are red.
3 out of every 7 apples are red.
qr.e: A 3:4 ratio means every group of 3 red apples comes with 4 green ones, so each group has 7 apples and 3 of those 7 are red.

qr.q: A drawing of a bookcase uses a scale of 1 inch to 2 feet. The bookcase is 3 inches tall in the drawing. How tall is the real bookcase?
qr.e: Each inch in the drawing stands for 2 feet, so 3 inches stands for 3 x 2 = 6 feet.

qr.q: On a park map, 2 centimeters represents 25 meters. A walking path is 14 centimeters long on the map. How long is the real path?
qr.e: 14 centimeters is 7 groups of 2 centimeters, and each 2 centimeters stands for 25 meters, so the path is 7 x 25 = 175 meters.

qr.q: A printer prints 8 pages every 20 seconds at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 3 minutes?
qr.e: Three minutes is 180 seconds, which is 9 groups of 20 seconds, so the printer prints 9 x 8 = 72 pages.

qr.q: A paint color mixes red, yellow, and white in the ratio 2:3:5. A painter uses 12 cups of yellow. How many cups of white are used?
qr.e: Yellow is 3 parts and equals 12 cups, so one part is 4 cups; white is 5 parts, or 5 x 4 = 20 cups.

qr.q: A model train is built at a scale of 1 inch to 8 feet. The real engine is 60 feet long. How long is the model?
qr.e: Each inch of the model stands for 8 feet, so the model is 60 divided by 8 = 7 1/2 inches long.

qr.q: A 15-ounce jar of honey costs $4.50. A 24-ounce jar of the same honey costs $6.72. Which jar is the better buy, and by how much per ounce?
c: The two jars cost the same per ounce
qr.e: $4.50 divided by 15 is $0.30 per ounce and $6.72 divided by 24 is $0.28 per ounce, so the 24-ounce jar saves $0.02 on every ounce.

qr.q: A recipe for 6 servings uses 3/4 cup of rice. Nadia has 2 cups of rice and plenty of everything else. What is the greatest number of whole servings she can make?
qr.e: One serving uses (3/4) divided by 6 = 1/8 cup, and 2 divided by 1/8 is 16, so she can make 16 servings.

qr.q: Ana stacks 24 boxes in 40 minutes. Ben stacks 21 boxes in 35 minutes. Each works at a steady rate. Which statement is true?
c: They stack at the same rate.
Ana stacks twice as fast as Ben.
qr.e: Ana stacks 24 divided by 40 = 0.6 box per minute and Ben stacks 21 divided by 35 = 0.6 box per minute, so their rates are equal.

qr.q: A scale drawing of a soccer field shows the field as a rectangle 12 centimeters long and 8 centimeters wide. What is the actual length of the field?
c: There is not enough information to tell.
qr.e: No scale is given, so there is nothing to tell how many meters each centimeter of the drawing stands for.

qr.q: A number pattern starts at 4 and adds 5 each time: 4, 9, 14, 19, ... . What is the next number in the pattern?
qr.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before it, so the next number is 19 + 5 = 24.

qr.q: Four bags of apples weigh 5 pounds, 7 pounds, 8 pounds, and 8 pounds. What is the mean weight of a bag?
qr.e: The four bags weigh 5 + 7 + 8 + 8 = 28 pounds in all, and 28 divided by 4 is 7 pounds.

qr.q: A backpack costs $40. During a sale the price drops 15%, and then a $5 coupon is used on the sale price. What is the final price?
qr.e: 15% of $40 is $6, so the sale price is $34, and $34 - $5 = $29.

qr.q: A bag holds 3 red tiles and 5 green tiles. One tile is drawn without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
qr.e: There are 3 + 5 = 8 tiles in all and 3 of them are red, so the probability is 3/8.

qr.q: A faucet fills a 3-gallon bucket in 4 minutes at a steady rate. How many minutes does it take to fill a 27-gallon tub?
qr.e: 27 gallons is 9 buckets of 3 gallons, and each bucket takes 4 minutes, so it takes 9 x 4 = 36 minutes.

qr.q: Of the 48 books on a shelf, 5/8 are novels. Of those novels, 2/5 are mysteries. How many of the books are mystery novels?
qr.e: 5/8 of 48 is 30 novels, and 2/5 of 30 is 12 mystery novels.

qr.q: Five plants were measured: 6 cm, 9 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm, and 5 cm. What is the median height?
qr.e: In order the heights are 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 cm, and the middle one of the five is 6 cm.

qr.q: Two friends share $84 in the ratio 3:4. How much more money does the friend with the larger share receive?
qr.e: Seven equal parts make $84, so each part is $12; the shares are $36 and $48, and the difference is one part, $12.

qr.q: Three corners of a rectangle are at (1, 1), (9, 1), and (9, 6). Where is the fourth corner?
qr.e: The side from (1, 1) to (9, 1) is horizontal and the side from (9, 1) to (9, 6) is vertical, so the fourth corner sits directly above (1, 1) at (1, 6).

qr.q: A pitcher holds 3 1/2 quarts of lemonade. Each glass holds 2/5 quart. How many full glasses can be poured, and how much lemonade is left over?
qr.e: 3 1/2 divided by 2/5 = 7/2 x 5/2 = 35/4 = 8 3/4, so 8 full glasses are poured, using 16/5 = 3 1/5 quarts and leaving 3 1/2 - 3 1/5 = 3/10 quart.

qr.q: Three times a number, decreased by 7, equals 26. What is half of that number?
qr.e: If 3n - 7 = 26, then 3n = 33 and n = 11, so half the number is 5 1/2.

qr.q: A rectangular box measures 12 cm by 8 cm by 6 cm. How many 2-cm cubes fit inside it exactly?
qr.e: Along the edges 6, 4, and 3 cubes fit (12/2, 8/2, and 6/2), so 6 x 4 x 3 = 72 cubes fill the box.

qr.q: On a floor plan, 3 inches represents 4 feet. A room is 18 feet long. How long is that room on the plan?
qr.e: 18 feet is 4.5 groups of 4 feet, and each 4 feet is drawn as 3 inches, so the room is 4.5 x 3 = 13 1/2 inches long.

qr.q: Kara's first four quiz scores have a mean of 78. What must she score on her fifth quiz to raise her mean to 80?
qr.e: Four quizzes with mean 78 total 312, and five quizzes with mean 80 must total 400, so the fifth score is 400 - 312 = 88.

qr.q: A rectangular garden is 8 meters by 15 meters. A path 1 meter wide is built all the way around the outside of the garden. What is the area of the path alone?
qr.e: With the path, the outer rectangle is 10 m by 17 m, or 170 square meters; subtracting the garden's 8 x 15 = 120 square meters leaves 50 square meters.

qr.q: What is the next multiple of 8 after 40?
qr.e: The multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, so the next one after 40 is 48.

qr.q: Which is the best estimate of 6,127 divided by 29?
qr.e: 6,127 is about 6,000 and 29 is about 30, and 6,000 divided by 30 is 200.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is a prime number?
qr.e: 17 has no whole-number factors except 1 and itself, while 9 = 3 x 3, 15 = 3 x 5, and 21 = 3 x 7.

qr.q: In the number 47,205, the value of the digit 4 is how many times the value of the digit 2?
qr.e: The 4 stands for 40,000 and the 2 stands for 200, and 40,000 divided by 200 is 200.

qr.q: Two consecutive whole numbers add up to 15. What is the larger of the two numbers?
qr.e: Consecutive whole numbers are 1 apart, and 7 + 8 = 15, so the larger number is 8.

qr.q: What is the sum of all the different prime factors of 210?
A student multiplied 397 x 18 and wrote 5,146. Without finding the exact product, which is the best reason to know that answer is wrong?
c: The product must be less than 4,000.
The product must end in the digit 7.
The product should be close to 7,200, not 5,146.
The product must be odd, and 5,146 is even.
qr.e: 397 is close to 400 and 400 x 18 = 7,200, so an answer near 5,100 is far too small; the exact product is 7,146.

qr.q: The four-digit number 73_4 is missing the digit in its tens place. If the number is divisible by 9, what is the missing digit?
qr.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digits add to a multiple of 9; 7 + 3 + 4 = 14, and 14 + 4 = 18, so the missing digit is 4 and the number is 7,344.

qr.q: A whole number rounds to 4,600 when it is rounded to the nearest hundred. What is the greatest whole number it could be?
qr.e: Whole numbers from 4,550 through 4,649 round to 4,600, and 4,650 would round up to 4,700, so the greatest is 4,649.

qr.q: Which of these numbers has exactly three different whole-number factors?
qr.e: 49 has only the factors 1, 7, and 49; 15 and 21 each have four factors, and 64 has seven.

qr.q: A whole number multiplied by itself equals 729. What is the number?
The sum of three whole numbers is odd. Which statement must be true?
c: Exactly two of the numbers are even.
Exactly one of the numbers is odd.
At least one of the numbers is odd.
qr.e: If all three numbers were even the sum would be even, so at least one must be odd; the sum is odd when either one number or all three are odd.

qr.q: Which of these fractions is equal to 1/2?
qr.e: 5/10 means 5 out of 10, which is exactly half; 2/5 and 3/8 are each less than half, and 4/6 is more than half.

qr.q: A theater has 80 seats, and 10% of them are already sold. How many seats are sold?
qr.e: 10% is the same as one tenth, and one tenth of 80 seats is 8 seats.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 6 but NOT by 9?
qr.e: 132 is even and its digits add to 6, a multiple of 3, so it is divisible by 6, but 6 is not a multiple of 9.

qr.q: What is the value of 2 x 2 x 2 x 5?
qr.e: Multiplying step by step, 2 x 2 = 4, then 4 x 2 = 8, and 8 x 5 = 40.

qr.q: A theater has 48 rows with 32 seats in each row. Which is the closest estimate of the total number of seats?
qr.e: 48 is about 50 and 32 is about 30, so the total is about 50 x 30 = 1,500; the exact product is 1,536.

qr.q: The mean of five numbers is 24. The number 40 is removed from the set. What is the mean of the four numbers that remain?
qr.e: Five numbers with mean 24 total 120; removing 40 leaves 80, and 80 divided by 4 is 20.

qr.q: In a triangle, one angle is a right angle and the other two angles measure 3x degrees and 2x degrees. What is the value of x?
qr.e: The three angles total 180 degrees, so 3x + 2x + 90 = 180, which gives 5x = 90 and x = 18.

qr.q: A set of five whole numbers has a median of 7 and a range of 5. The smallest number is 5. What is the largest number?
c: There is not enough information to tell.
qr.e: The range is the largest number minus the smallest, so the largest is 5 + 5 = 10; the median does not change that.

qr.q: A model car is built at 1/24 of the size of the real car. The model is 7 inches long. How long is the real car, in feet?
qr.e: The real car is 24 x 7 = 168 inches long, and 168 divided by 12 is 14 feet.

qr.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
qr.e: 5/8 = 0.625 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so the correct order is 0.6, then 5/8, then 2/3, then 0.7.

qr.q: A machine fills 350 bottles in 25 minutes at a steady rate. At that rate, how many bottles does it fill in 1 hour and 20 minutes?
qr.e: 350 divided by 25 is 14 bottles per minute, and 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes, so 80 x 14 = 1,120 bottles.

qr.q: A jacket costs $60. The store raises the price by 25%, then later takes 20% off the new price. What is the final price?
qr.e: A 25% increase makes the price $75, and 20% of $75 is $15, so the final price is $75 - $15 = $60.

qr.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 square centimeters and a perimeter of 36 centimeters. What are its side lengths?
qr.e: The two sides must add to 18, half of the perimeter, and multiply to 72; 6 + 12 = 18 and 6 x 12 = 72.

qr.q: When a whole number is divided by 7, the remainder is 4. What is the remainder when twice that number is divided by 7?
qr.e: Doubling adds the remainder to itself: 4 + 4 = 8, and 8 is one more than 7, so the new remainder is 1 (for example, 11 leaves 4 and 22 leaves 1).

qr.q: Which of these statements is FALSE?
c: The product of two even numbers is always divisible by 8.
The sum of an even number and an odd number is always odd.
The sum of two odd numbers is always even.
The product of two odd numbers is always odd.
qr.e: 2 x 2 = 4, which is not divisible by 8, so the last statement is false; the other three are always true.

qr.q: A square photo frame has sides that are 7 inches long. What is the perimeter of the frame?
qr.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28 inches.

qr.q: A box is filled with unit cubes. Each layer holds 8 cubes, and the box is 3 layers tall. How many unit cubes does the box hold in all?
qr.e: Three layers of 8 cubes each is 3 × 8 = 24 cubes.

qr.q: A rectangular tank is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 6 inches deep. Water in it is 3 inches deep. How many more cubic inches of water are needed to fill the tank?
qr.e: The tank holds 8×5×6=240 cubic inches and already has 8×5×3=120, so 240−120=120 more are needed.

qr.q: The ages of nine students are listed in order: 8, 9, 9, 10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 13. What is the median age?
qr.e: With nine values listed in order, the median is the 5th one, and the 5th age in the list is 10.

qr.q: A shop records books sold: Monday 12, Tuesday 18, Wednesday 9, Thursday 15, Friday 21. The goal was to average 16 books per day over the five days. How many more books would the shop have had to sell that week to meet the goal?
qr.e: The shop sold 12+18+9+15+21=75 books, but the goal needed 5×16=80, so it fell 5 books short.

qr.q: One week of daily high temperatures has a range of 14°. The next week, every daily high is exactly 5° warmer than the matching day of the first week. What is the range of the second week's highs?
qr.e: Adding 5° to every value raises the highest and the lowest by the same amount, so the range stays 14°.

qr.q: In a pictograph, one book symbol stands for 8 books read. Grade 4 shows 5 1/2 symbols and Grade 5 shows 7 symbols. How many more books did Grade 5 read than Grade 4?
qr.e: Grade 5 read 7×8=56 books and Grade 4 read 5 1/2×8=44, so the difference is 56−44=12.

qr.q: Two rectangular pens each use exactly 24 meters of fencing. Pen 1 measures 4 m by 8 m and Pen 2 measures 6 m by 6 m. How much greater is the area of Pen 2?
qr.e: Both perimeters are 24 m, but the areas are 4×8=32 and 6×6=36, so Pen 2 is 36−32=4 square meters larger.

qr.q: Bag X holds 4 red and 8 blue marbles. Bag Y holds 3 red and 5 blue marbles. From which bag is drawing a red marble more likely?
c: Bag X, because it has more red marbles
Bag X, because it holds more marbles in all
Bag Y, because 3/8 is greater than 1/3
qr.e: Bag X gives 4/12=1/3 and Bag Y gives 3/8; since 1/3=8/24 and 3/8=9/24, Bag Y is more likely.

qr.q: A rug is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide. A second rug is 3 times as long and half as wide as the first. How does the area of the second rug compare with the area of the first?
qr.e: The first rug covers 6×4=24 sq ft; the second is 18 by 2, or 36 sq ft, and 36÷24=1 1/2. Tripling one side and halving the other multiplies the area by 3×1/2.

qr.q: The mean of five numbers is 14. A sixth number is added, and the mean of all six numbers is 15. What is the sixth number?
qr.e: The five numbers total 5×14=70 and all six total 6×15=90, so the added number is 90−70=20.

qr.q: In a triangle, two of the angles are equal and the third angle is 30° larger than each of them. What is the measure of the largest angle?
qr.e: If each equal angle is x, then x+x+(x+30)=180, so 3x=150 and x=50; the largest angle is 50+30=80°.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 5?
qr.e: A whole number is divisible by 5 when its last digit is 0 or 5, and 75 ends in 5 while the others end in 2, 8, and 4.

qr.q: A rope is 4 feet long. How many inches long is the rope? (1 foot = 12 inches)
qr.e: Each foot is 12 inches, so 4 feet is 4 × 12 = 48 inches.

qr.q: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes?
qr.e: The rate is 42÷6=7 pages per minute, so in 15 minutes it prints 7×15=105 pages.

qr.q: The numbers in a pattern are 45, 40, 35, 30, ... . What is the next number in the pattern?
qr.e: Each number is 5 less than the one before it, so the next number is 30 − 5 = 25.

qr.q: A jacket priced at $80 is marked down 25%. At the register, another $5 is taken off. What is the final price?
qr.e: 25% of $80 is $20, so the marked-down price is $60, and $60−$5=$55.

qr.q: A team records its goals each week: Week 1 has 4 goals, Week 2 has 7 goals, Week 3 has 5 goals, and Week 4 has 6 goals. How many goals did the team score in the four weeks altogether?
qr.e: Adding the four weeks gives 4 + 7 + 5 + 6 = 22 goals.

qr.q: Ten cards numbered 1 through 10 are placed face down and one is drawn at random. What is the probability that the card drawn shows a prime number?
qr.e: The primes from 1 to 10 are 2, 3, 5, and 7 — four of the ten cards — so the probability is 4/10=2/5.

qr.q: Which fraction is between 1/3 and 1/2?
qr.e: In twelfths, 1/3=4/12 and 1/2=6/12, and 5/12 falls between them; 1/4 is smaller and 3/5 and 2/3 are larger than 1/2.

qr.q: Priya has 5/8 of a yard of ribbon but needs 2/3 of a yard. How much more ribbon does she need?
qr.e: Using 24ths, 2/3=16/24 and 5/8=15/24, so she needs 16/24−15/24=1/24 of a yard.

qr.q: A rectangular sheet of paper is 10 cm by 6 cm. A 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle is cut away from one corner. What is the area of the piece that is left?
qr.e: The whole sheet is 10×6=60 square cm and the piece removed is 3×4=12, so 60−12=48 square cm remain.

qr.q: Three vertices of a rectangle are (1, 5), (9, 5), and (9, 2). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex?
qr.e: The fourth vertex shares the x-value 1 with (1, 5) and the y-value 2 with (9, 2), giving (1, 2).

qr.q: A stadium sold 4,180 tickets on Friday, 3,905 on Saturday, and 2,870 on Sunday. Which is the best estimate of the total number of tickets sold?
qr.e: Rounding gives 4,200+3,900+2,900=11,000, and the exact total, 10,955, is much closer to 11,000 than to 10,000.

qr.q: Three pencils and two erasers cost $1.30 in all. One pencil costs $0.30. What does one eraser cost?
qr.e: The pencils cost 3×$0.30=$0.90, leaving $1.30−$0.90=$0.40 for two erasers, so one eraser is $0.20.

qr.q: A student's five test scores have a mean of 82. If the lowest score, 62, is dropped, what is the mean of the four remaining scores?
qr.e: The five scores total 5×82=410; without the 62 the total is 348, and 348÷4=87.

qr.q: In a class, the ratio of students who walk to school to students who ride is 2:5. There are 21 more riders than walkers. How many students are in the class?
qr.e: The difference is 5−2=3 parts, so one part is 21÷3=7 students; the class has 2+5=7 parts, or 7×7=49 students.

qr.q: There are 38 cookies packed into bags of 5. After all the full bags are made, how many cookies are left over?
qr.e: Seven full bags use 7 × 5 = 35 cookies, and 38 − 35 = 3 cookies are left over.

qr.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices, and 3 of the slices are eaten. What fraction of the pizza is left?
qr.e: Three of the 8 slices are gone, so 8 − 3 = 5 slices remain, which is 5/8 of the pizza.

qr.q: Dana has $20 and wants to buy items priced $6.85, $4.20, and $7.95. Which statement is true?
c: She can buy all three and have $1.00 left
She can buy all three with exactly $0 left
She can buy all three and have $2.00 left

qr.q: Which is the best estimate of 4,982 ÷ 51?
qr.e: Rounding gives 5,000÷50=100, and the exact quotient is a little under 98, so 100 is the closest estimate.

qr.q: Four friends have a mean score of 20 in a game. A fifth friend joins with a score of 25. What is the mean score of all five friends?
qr.e: The four friends total 4×20=80, so all five total 105, and 105÷5=21.

qr.q: How many 1-centimeter cubes are needed to fill a box that is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall?
qr.e: Each layer holds 5 × 3 = 15 cubes and the box is 2 layers tall, so 15 × 2 = 30 cubes fill it.

qr.q: On a scale drawing, 3 cm represents 12 meters. A hallway is actually 30 meters long. How long is that hallway on the drawing?
qr.e: Since 3 cm stands for 12 m, 1 cm stands for 4 m, so 30 m needs 30÷4=7.5 cm.

qr.q: Car A travels 150 miles on 5 gallons of gas. Car B travels 210 miles on 7 gallons. Which car goes farther on one gallon?
c: Car A, at 35 miles per gallon
Car B, at 30 miles per gallon
Car B, because it traveled more miles
Neither — both travel 30 miles per gallon
qr.e: 150÷5=30 and 210÷7=30, so the two cars have exactly the same rate of 30 miles per gallon.

qr.q: A spinner has 20 equal sections, and each section is either green or white. The probability of landing on green is 2/5. How many of the sections are white?
qr.e: Two fifths of the 20 sections is 8 green sections, so the other 20 − 8 = 12 sections are white.

qr.q: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The rectangle measures 12 cm by 4 cm. What is the area of the square?
qr.e: The rectangle's perimeter is 2(12+4)=32 cm, so the square has side 32÷4=8 cm and area 8×8=64 square cm.

qr.q: The $60 price of a game is raised by 10%, and the new price is later lowered by 10%. What is the final price?
qr.e: The price rises to $66, and 10% of $66 is $6.60, so the final price is $66−$6.60=$59.40 — less than the original because the second 10% is taken from a larger number.

qr.q: Elena spent 2/5 of her money on a book, then spent 1/3 of what was left on a snack. She has $12 left. How much money did she start with?
qr.e: After the book, 3/5 remains; spending 1/3 of that leaves 2/3 × 3/5 = 2/5 of the start, so 2/5 of the money is $12 and the whole is $30.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is the greatest?
qr.e: Written as decimals, 3/5=0.6 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so 0.7 is greater than all the others, including 0.68.

qr.q: In a survey, 35 out of 50 students chose soccer. What percent of the students chose soccer?
qr.e: 35/50 = 70/100, so 70% of the students chose soccer.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is NOT divisible by 6?
qr.e: A number divisible by 6 must be even and have a digit sum divisible by 3; 358 is even but 3+5+8=16 is not a multiple of 3, while 132, 246, and 414 pass both tests.

qr.q: A list of numbers is 3, 7, 3, 9, and 5. What is the mode of the list?
qr.e: The mode is the value that appears most often, and 3 appears twice while each of the others appears once.

qr.q: What is the median of 4, 9, 11, 15, 6, and 20?
qr.e: In order the values are 4, 6, 9, 11, 15, 20; with six values the median is the mean of the middle two, (9+11)÷2=10.

qr.q: A number pattern counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, ... . What is the 6th number in the pattern?
qr.e: Counting on by 3s gives 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, so the 6th number in the pattern is 18.

qr.q: How many cubes with edges of 2 cm fit exactly inside a box that is 8 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm?
qr.e: Along the edges the cubes fit 4 by 3 by 2, so 4×3×2=24 cubes fill the box.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is a factor of 15?
qr.e: 15 = 3 × 5, so 5 divides 15 with nothing left over, while 2, 4, and 6 do not.

qr.q: Two angles are complementary, and one of them is twice as large as the other. What is the measure of the larger angle?
qr.e: Complementary angles total 90°, so x+2x=90 gives x=30° and the larger angle is 2×30=60°.

qr.q: Which is greater, 3 × 3 × 3 or 5 × 5, and by how much?
A jar holds 15 buttons: 6 are blue, 4 are white, and 5 are black. One button is taken out without looking. What is the probability that it is black?
qr.e: There are 15 buttons in all and 5 of them are black, so the probability is 5/15, which is the same as 1/3.

qr.q: Five boxes each hold the same number of books. When 3 more books are added to the collection, there are 43 books in all. How many books are in each box?
qr.e: If each box holds b books, then 5b+3=43, so 5b=40 and b=8.

qr.q: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width. If the perimeter is 48 cm, what is the width?
qr.e: With width w the length is 3w, so the perimeter is 2(3w+w)=8w=48, giving w=6 cm (and length 18 cm).

qr.q: Notebooks cost $2.95 each. Maya has $20 and no coupon. What is the greatest number of notebooks she can buy?
qr.e: Rounding $2.95 up to $3 gives about 6 notebooks; checking, 6 cost $17.70 and 7 would cost $20.65, which is more than $20.

qr.q: A rectangular pool measures 10 m by 6 m. A walkway 2 m wide is built all the way around it. What is the area of the walkway alone?
qr.e: The pool plus walkway measures 14 m by 10 m, or 140 square meters, and the pool covers 60, so the walkway is 140−60=80 square meters.

ma.q: A garden is 6 m by 3 m. What fencing length goes around it?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(6+3) = 18 m.

ma.q: A triangular flag has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
A roof triangle has angles 45° and 60°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 75°.

ma.q: A square patio has side length 10 units. What is its area?
A banner is 10 cm by 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(10+3) = 26 cm.

ma.q: A triangular flag has base 10 cm and height 8 cm. What is its area?
A sail triangle has angles 65° and 55°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 60°.

ma.q: A square mosaic has side length 7 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 7² = 49.

ma.q: A pen is 8 cm by 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(8+3) = 22 cm.

ma.q: A triangular sign has base 10 cm and height 4 cm. What is its area?
A roof triangle has angles 45° and 75°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 60°.

ma.q: A square game board has side length 4 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 4² = 16.

ma.q: A $100 item is 75% off. What is its sale price?
What is 5.5÷0.1?

ma.q: Solve 3x+5=83.

ma.q: Four tenths of 70 teams earn a badge. How many teams earn a badge?
ma.e: Four tenths of 70 is 28.

ma.q: A square stage has side length 9 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area=9²=81.

ma.q: What is 160÷2?

ma.q: What is 25% of 88?
ma.e: One fourth of 88 is 22.

What is 3/4 of 48?
What is 5×13?
2.5 feet equals how many inches?
What is 7×8?
A storage box measures 6×2×2. What is its volume?
A poster is 3 feet long. How many inches is that?

ma.e: The sum is 174; divide by 3 to get 58.

ma.q: What is the median of 53,56,59,62,66?
ma.e: The ordered middle value is 59.

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 56,59,59,61,64?

ma.q: An aquarium measures 6×3×4. What is its volume?
An 8-foot rope is how many inches long?

ma.q: What is the mean of readings 59,63,67?

ma.q: What is the median of 58,61,64,67,71?

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 61,64,64,66,69?
ma.e: 64 occurs most often.

ma.q: A crate measures 7×5×4. What is its volume?
A block measures 3×2×2. What is its volume?

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 66,69,69,71,74?

ma.q: What is the mean of 67,71,75?

ma.q: What is the median of 66,69,72,75,79?
